topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and their genetic basis
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s learning outcomes and its use of cancer hallmarks to connect mutations with changes in tissue behavior.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and survival signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways make cancer cells less dependent on growth stimulation and less responsive to growth inhibition.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation changes the identity and organization of cancer cells relative to their normal maturation pathways.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered p53 signaling and the balance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to evade cell death.

topics.label: Replicative limits, senescence and cancer-cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the safeguards that limit continued cell division and how cancer cells overcome them, concluding with a recap of growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine altered cancer metabolism as a functional adaptation that both reflects and reinforces molecular changes in tumors.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit a blood supply to overcome the limits of oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and successful colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells reach distant sites and what determines whether they survive there to form detectable metastases.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture’s learning outcomes, emphasizes convergence on shared hallmarks, and offers further reading before the farewell.
